# Batch operations

## When to use this guide

You need to push or pull many blobs from a shell script (e.g. CI bootstrap)
and want maximum throughput without exceeding rate limits.

## Bulk upload with `xargs -P`

```bash
find ./outputs -type f -print0 \
  | xargs -0 -n1 -P 32 corelink put --output json \
  | jq -r '.digest' > digests.txt
```

`-P 32` is a safe default; server allows up to `256` per PAT.

## Bulk download

```bash
while read -r digest; do
  corelink get "$digest" -o "blobs/$digest"
done < digests.txt
```

For parallel downloads:

```bash
cat digests.txt \
  | xargs -n1 -P 32 -I {} corelink get {} -o "blobs/{}"
```

## Rate-limit handling

`corelink` exits `5` on `COR_QUOTA_RATELIMIT`. A back-off loop:

```bash
attempt=0
until corelink put "$file"; do
  rc=$?
  [[ $rc -ne 5 ]] && exit $rc       # non-rate-limit failure: bail
  attempt=$((attempt+1))
  [[ $attempt -ge 5 ]] && exit 5    # give up
  sleep $((2 ** attempt))           # 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s
done
```

In real scripts use one of the SDKs which implement this loop natively.

## Pre-dedupe with `b3sum`

```bash
declare -A seen
while IFS= read -r file; do
  digest=$(b3sum "$file" | awk '{print $1}')
  [[ -n "${seen[$digest]:-}" ]] && continue
  seen[$digest]=1
  corelink put "$file" --digest "$digest"
done < files.txt
```

Cuts upload count by 60-90% on typical build outputs.
